business_problem: Lloyds Banking Group wanted to move beyond siloed AI pilots and scale generative AI across a large regulated bank, but it needed a governed architecture, self-service delivery model, and robust safeguards before business and technology teams could take AI solutions from concept to production at enterprise scale.
solution_summary: Lloyds Banking Group expanded its relationship with TCS to stand up a GenAI Office and a shared enterprise AI operating environment rather than launching isolated experiments. TCS assessed the bank's business and technology stack, then defined the architecture and roadmap for a secure, scalable foundation that connects the bank's data estate with self-service access to GenAI products and models. The GenAI Office acts as the orchestration layer for demand, standards, and rollout, while frameworks and guardrails govern how teams build, deploy, and operate new AI solutions from concept to production. This lets colleagues across customer engagement, product innovation, engineering, colleague support, and operations reuse approved capabilities instead of recreating their own tooling, turning generative AI into a managed enterprise platform with explicit ownership and control points.

Business and technology teams self-serve approved GenAI products and models, while frameworks and guardrails control how new solutions move from concept to production and into customer, engineering, colleague, and operations workflows.
business_outcome: Lloyds Banking Group created a governed enterprise GenAI foundation that has already delivered dozens of live use cases and measurable financial value, while giving teams a faster path to build AI into customer, employee, engineering, and operational workflows without losing control over governance or cost.
